title: State machine document
description: states.json — an XState v5 machine configuration describing the state of one conversation as the protocol sees it, not the internal state of any participant. Pinned to a subset that createMachine() accepts verbatim. Specified in framework/spec/kinds/protocol.md; validated by framework/portal/src/lib/protocol/states.ts.

id.description: MUST equal the protocol entity's name (E_PROTO_STATES_ID). It is also the root of every absolute target path, e.g. #order-placement.rejected.

initial.description: A key of this object's own states.

state.description: A state node. `additionalProperties: false` is where the subset is enforced: context, assign, always, after, invoke, input, output and meta have no member here, and any of them is E_PROTO_STATES_SUBSET. The catalog documents contracts, not runtime behaviour — anything carrying data or executing is out.

initial.description: REQUIRED if and only if this node has states — a compound state must say where it begins.

type.description: The only legal value. type: parallel and type: history are outside the subset. A final state MUST carry no `on`.

transitions.description: Event name to transition. Event names MUST match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ (E_PROTO_STATES_EVENT_NAME), which excludes the wildcard "*" by construction. An event name maps to a workflow message name by lowercasing and turning _ into -; one with no such message anywhere in the protocol's workflows raises W_PROTO_STATES_EVENT_UNKNOWN.

transition-value.description: A target string, a transition object, or an array of transition objects evaluated top to bottom — first matching guard wins, and an unguarded entry is the fallback.

guard.description: A plain string, rendered as [guard] on the edge. Object-form guards are outside the subset.

target.description: Exactly two forms (E_PROTO_STATES_TARGET otherwise): a sibling state key such as "reserved", or an absolute id path such as "#order-placement.rejected". Relative descent ("reserved.settled") is not supported — it is the form that most often silently resolves to the wrong node. Omitting target entirely makes the transition an internal self-transition: actions run, the machine does not move.

actions.description: Action names as plain strings. Object-form actions, and assign in particular, are outside the subset — they carry data, and data shapes belong to datamodels.
